record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: For general n, is CP_n facially exposed? Here CP_n is the cone of real symmetric n x n matrices A = B B^T for some entrywise nonnegative matrix B. A face F of a closed convex cone K is exposed if there is a nonzero symmetric matrix C such that K is contained in the half-space {X : trace(CX) >= 0} and F = {X in K : trace(CX) = 0}; K is facially exposed if every face is exposed.

evidence.quote: It is unknown whether CPn is facially exposed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n\geq 1$, let $\mathcal{S}^n$ denote the space of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices, equipped with the trace inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle = \operatorname{trace}(XY)$. Define the completely positive cone
$$\mathrm{CP}_n = \{A\in \mathcal{S}^n : A = BB^T \text{ for some entrywise nonnegative matrix } B \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k},\ k\geq 1\}.$$
$\mathrm{CP}_n$ is a closed convex cone in $\mathcal{S}^n$. A face $F$ of a closed convex cone $K\subseteq \mathcal{S}^n$ is called exposed if there exists a nonzero $C\in \mathcal{S}^n$ such that $\langle C,X\rangle \geq 0$ for all $X\in K$ and $F = \{X\in K : \langle C,X\rangle = 0\}$. The cone $K$ is facially exposed if every face of $K$ is exposed.

Determine, for each integer $n\geq 1$, whether $\mathrm{CP}_n$ is facially exposed.
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been resolved in the negative. Zhang (Linear Algebra and its Applications, 2018, "Completely positive cones: Are they facially exposed?") exhibited a class of non-exposed faces of $\mathrm{CP}_5$, showing that $\mathrm{CP}_5$ is not facially exposed; by embedding $\mathrm{CP}_5$ into $\mathrm{CP}_n$ for $n>5$, $\mathrm{CP}_n$ fails to be facially exposed for all $n\geq 5$. For small $n\leq 4$, $\mathrm{CP}_n$ coincides with the doubly nonnegative cone and is facially exposed.

status_evidence.title: Completely positive cones: Are they facially exposed?
status_evidence.snippet: A class of non-exposed faces of the 5×5 completely positive cone is identified, which implies that the 5×5 completely positive cone is not facially exposed; by embedding it into CP_n for n>5, CP_n is not facially exposed for n>5.
status_evidence.claim: CP_n is not facially exposed for n>=5.

status_evidence.title: Faces of the 5 × 5 completely positive cone
status_evidence.snippet: Study of the facial structure of the 5×5 completely positive cone.
status_evidence.claim: Related work analyzing faces of CP_5.
